Equipment responsibility guide

Our tracking page records three different stages for imported parcels. CUSTOMS RELEASED means the authorities have allowed the parcel to enter the country. It does not mean Eastline has collected it. RECEIVED BY LOCAL CARRIER appears only after our depot scans the parcel during handover. OUT FOR DELIVERY means it has been loaded onto a delivery vehicle.

If the page shows only CUSTOMS RELEASED, please allow time for the handover scan before asking for a delivery appointment. The appointment tool opens when RECEIVED BY LOCAL CARRIER appears. A customs reference number cannot be used to arrange an appointment because it belongs to a separate system.

Example: Parcel EL62 was released at 08:15 and scanned at our depot at 13:40. Its recipient could book an appointment after 13:40, although the parcel had not yet been loaded for delivery. A vehicle assignment is shown separately; the appointment screen does not itself prove that a driver has the parcel.

Inventory Count Exception Procedure

Each Friday, storekeepers compare shelf quantities with the inventory system. If a difference is found, a second employee must recount the item before any stock record is amended.

Give the second counter the item code and shelf location, but do not reveal the first count or the quantity shown in the system. The second count must be completed independently.

The supervisor will reconcile any difference by comparing the counts with the dated receipt and withdrawal logs. When two independent counts match and the movement records have been checked, the supervisor may update the stock record. If the counts disagree, an experienced employee must make a third count before the discrepancy can be resolved.

Submit the count sheet and the movement records together. Changing the system quantity before verification is not permitted.

The clear aisle beside every stand must remain 1.5 metres wide throughout public opening hours. Exhibition Safety Team

COORDINATING HEALTH BENEFITS — Staff Notice

If you are covered as an employee by one plan and as a spouse's dependent by another, your own employee plan pays first. The plan with the higher annual limit does not automatically become the first payer. Send the first plan's settlement statement with any claim to the second plan.

The second plan considers the eligible amount still unpaid after the first settlement, subject to its own benefit limit. It does not pay the whole original bill again. Combined payments must not exceed the eligible bill. A larger annual limit is a ceiling on potential benefits, not a promise that the plan will pay first or pay every claim in full.
